title: Small-session spectra: latency vs cost annotated draft
content:
Purpose:
This note collects a compact set of microbenchmarks focused on small-session traffic shapes (1–8 tokens per request, high QPS, >90% short sessions). Goal: produce a short, shareable artifact for Console + Optimize teams to reason about tradeoffs between latency SLOs and $/q for micro-interactions (chat typing, autosuggest, short completions).

Background & motivation:
- Many customer workloads are dominated by extremely short envelopes: assistant suggestion, one-shot Q&A, or completion snippets. Traditional batching and tiling heuristics optimized for longer sequences can worsen p99 for these microcalls while increasing cost due to idle slot occupancy.
- We want to surface a simple spectrum of small-session operating points to help Console expose knobs (small-session fastpath, compact-quantize, ultra-prefetch) with approximate unit economics.

Workload definition:
- Payload: text-only, average length 3 tokens (sd 1.2), max 8 tokens
- Request profile: poisson arrival, mean inter-arrival set to achieve per-GPU offered load at tested QPS points: 2k, 5k, 10k
- Model variants: base-fp16, int8-quant (QAT-like profile), int4-compact (aggressive quant), and a distilled smaller L2 model
- Serving modes: immediate-single (no batching), small-window batching (40ms window), slot-tiling (4-slot multiplex), kv-prefetch enabled/disabled
- Metrics captured: p50, p90, p95, p99 latency (ms), tokens/second throughput, $/query (amortized based on experimental GPU cost model), CPU overhead, KV-cache hit rate

Test matrix (abbrev):
- Models: FP16 | INT8 | INT4 | DISTILLED
- Modes: IMMED | SW40 | TILING4 | TILING4+PREFETCH
- QPS points: 2k | 5k | 10k
- Each cell = 5 runs x 60s, median reported

Observations from table (5k QPS):
- For ultra-short requests, immediate-single (no batching) frequently gives the best tail p99 compared to windowed batching; batching increases p50/p90/p99 even when it improves $/q slightly.
- Tiling with small multiplex (TILING4) recovers much of batching's $/q without as large a p99 penalty, especially when paired with a compact quant path (int4).
- Prefetching KV when session affinity can be predicted yields best combined p99 and $/q; we saw noticeable p99 drops and modest cost increases only when prefetch misses are frequent.
- Distilled models are attractive on pure $/q but can increase p99 under contention unless paired with fastpath scheduling.

ASCII chart: p99 latency vs $/q across modes at 5k QPS (each row = a mode+model point). Lower-left is ideal (low latency, low cost).
Legend: x-axis = $/q (0.0015 -> 0.0045), y-axis = p99 latency (ms, 0 -> 220). Rough scatter rendered as text.

Scale: x cols 50 chars representing $/q min..max (0.0015..0.0045) ; y rows 12 representing 0..220ms

(Interpretation: cluster on left are int4/distil TILING modes with lower $/q; upper-right are FP16 SW40 batch modes with high p99 + high $/q.)

Micro-insights (behavioral patterns across QPS sweep):
- At 2k QPS: IMMED p99 advantage is small (roughly 10–15ms gain) vs tiling; $/q differences are muted because GPU slot occupancy low.
- At 10k QPS: IMMED p99 tail balloons (queueing effect) and $/q rises for IMMED; tiling and SW40 maintain lower $/q but p99 depends on multiplex arbitration.
- Int4 shows best $/q across QPS but is more sensitive to transient CPU scheduling jitter (we saw p95 spikes when host CPU hit 60% util).
- KV-prefetch helps only when session reuse > 10% within short windows; otherwise prefetch cost dominates and $/q increases without latency benefit.

Operational notes / anomalies seen in runs:
- Run 4 of FP16 SW40 at 5k had a node-level GC pause (observed in logs): artificially high p99; removed from median aggregation but flagged in notes.
- TILING4 scheduling occasionally starved single-slot requests when multiplex share was 80/20 skewed. Need fairness tuning (ticket JIRA-OPS-1127).
- Measurement jitter for p99 can be +/- 8–12ms across 60s runs; recommend 3-minute runs for final claim set.

Suggested Console surface ideas (for product teams):
- "Small-session fastpath" toggle: enables IMMED priority for requests under 6 tokens but with a circuit-breaker when queue depth > threshold. Show expected p99 delta and approximate $/q delta in the UI based on recent traffic.
- "Compact mode" per-route: allow an int4 or distilled fallback with quick opt-in; show quality tradeoff link and a projected cost bar.
- Prefetch slider: allow customers to set prefetch aggressiveness; show recent hit-rate and estimated amortized cost.

Next steps / experiments to stabilize:
- Re-run the full matrix with 3x longer windows (180s) and 10k-run sample to tighten p99 CI (owner: Alexei).
- Calibrate CPU-side jitter mitigation: pin scheduler for compact-quant worker processes (owner: Priya).
- Small closed beta: expose fastpath toggle to two customers with short-session heavy traffic and collect real telemet (owner: Samir).
- Follow-up PR to runtime: fairness fallback for tiling when request size < 8 tokens (see PR #456 for initial patch).

Questions for reviewers:
- Are we comfortable exposing immediate-single as an explicit product knob or should it remain an internal scheduling policy?
- What level of accuracy are product teams willing to accept for $/q estimates (rounded to 10% vs 5%)?
- Any additional telemetry signals we should capture before beta (session age, client retry count, encoding overhead)?

- Slack thread: #runtime-benchmarks, 2027-06-16, "small-session spectra initial"

Notes to self: keep this artifact short and linked to a Confluence page with plots for the executive brief. This should be shareable with Optimize and Console folks as a draft — expect to iterate.

-- Maya
